On Sun, Dec 30, 2012 at 7:28 PM, sania <sans...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Hi,
>
> I am using the this code to make forest plots, I want to make a change that
> is regarding geom_point(), I want to give different size to each point based
> on separate number for each point i.e. number of obsearvations, pls. help.

Use the size aesthetic in geom_point(). You didn't provide an example
with data, but here is a Q & D version that illustrates the idea:

DF <- data.frame(x = 1:10, y = 1:10, n = sample(50, 10))
require(ggplot2)
ggplot(DF, aes(x, y)) + geom_point(aes(size = n))

Observe that a doubling of n results in a fourfold increase in the
area of the dot. A better way is to use scale_size_area() [in the
current version 0.9.3] or scale_area() [in previous versions]:

ggplot(DF, aes(x, y)) + geom_point(aes(size = n)) + scale_size_area()

The documentation hasn't caught up yet, but if you try scale_area() in
the current version, you'll get a warning that scale_area is
deprecated.

Dennis

Hi Sania,
 
Here is the code for a reproducible example on forest plot, which I (as a beginner ggplot user) had written in the past with some input from Dennis.  Thanks to him.
 
Please ignore if this does not serve your purpose.
 
Thnaks,
 
Pradip Muhuri
#####
setwd ('E:/')
library(ggplot2)
dat <- read.table (text="
a18_34,s,     3.53, 2.31, 5.39
a18_34,sd,   3.39, 2.19, 5.25
a18_34,sdc,   2.78, 1.76, 4.38
a18_34,sdcsb, 2.52, 1.6, 3.99
a35_54,s,     2.96, 2.51, 3.49
a35_54,sd,   2.53, 2.15, 2.99
a35_54,sdc,   1.6, 1.33, 1.92
a35_54,sdcsb, 1.38, 1.14, 1.66
a55p,s,       1.84, 1.68, 2.02
a55p,sd,     1.65, 1.49, 1.81
a55p,sdc,     1.35, 1.23, 1.49
a55p,sdcsb,   1.31, 1.19, 1.45",
sep=",",
col.names=c('age', 'Model', 'Est','LCI','UCI'),                
colClasses=c('character', 'character', 'numeric', 'numeric','numeric'))
               
  #chracter to factor
  dat$age <- factor(dat$age, levels=c ('a18_34','a35_54', 'a55p'),
                     labels=c('18-34', '35-54', '55 or Older'))
  
  dat$Model <- factor(dat$Model,levels=c('s', 'sd','sdc', 'sdcsb'),
                        labels=c('SPD Only',
                                 'SPD, Adj for SDE',
                                 'SPD, Adj for SDE & CHR',
                                 'SPD, Adj for SDE, CHR, BMI & SMK'))    
  dat
p <- ggplot(dat, aes(x=Model, y=Est, ymin=LCI, ymax=UCI))+
    geom_pointrange(linetype = 1,size=1.0, colour = "navyblue")+
    geom_hline(aes(yintercept=1), size=1.0, colour="red", lty=2) +
       facet_wrap(~ age, nrow=1)+
    coord_flip()+
    ylim(0,6.0)+
    scale_fill_grey()+ theme_bw()+
    xlab ("  ")+
    ylab("  ")+
   
                  
theme(text = element_text(size = 25, face = "bold"),
plot.background = element_rect (),
axis.text.x = element_text(vjust = 1.5, size=18,face="bold"),
axis.text.y = element_text(hjust = 1, size=18, face="bold"),
axis.title.y = element_text(hjust=1, size = rel(0.4), face="bold"),
axis.title.x = element_text(vjust=1, size = 20, face = "bold"),
strip.text.x = element_text (size=20, face="bold"),
legend.text = element_text(size = rel(0.4), hjust = 0),
legend.position = "none"
)
print(p)
ggsave(file='test_forest_plots_hr.png', width=11, height=7)

On Sunday, December 30, 2012 10:28:20 PM UTC-5, sania wrote:

Hi,

I am using the this code to make forest plots, I want to make a change that is regarding geom_point(), I want to give different size to each point based on separate number for each point i.e. number of obsearvations, pls. help.

d <- read.csv("test1.csv")
forestplot <- function(d, xlab="RR", ylab="test1"){
  require(ggplot2)
  p <- ggplot(d, aes(x=x, y=y, ymin=ylo, ymax=yhi)) +
    coord_flip()+
    geom_point() + geom_errorbar(width=0.2)+
     geom_hline(aes(x=0), lty=2) +
    ylab(xlab) +
    xlab(ylab) #switch because of the coord_flip() above
  return(p)
}
forestplot(d)

thank you,
sania
